body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. The story leading the day is a homecoming: Todd Lee, who helped bring a national championship to CSUB three decades ago, is back as head coach of Roadrunners basketball, and he's talking as much about the city as the scoreboard. Outside, expect a mild fall Tuesday — a high near 73, a low around 50 tonight, moderate air quality, and no weather alerts for Kern County. Fire crews remain on one active fire in the county, the Cyrus Fire.

## The Kern Overnight

The biggest call of the night came on the southbound Highway 204 connector onto Highway 99, where a single vehicle rolled over. Fire crews reported four patients, all tagged green for minor injuries, and called for a second ambulance to the scene. One engine was canceled once things were under control. No names or exact locations beyond the connector were released.

Elsewhere in the county, a vehicle hit the front of the mountain and rolled over on northbound Highway 155 in the Kern River canyon, about a mile south of Hungry Gulch. Radio traffic described poor cell phone reception with the patient, and the wrecked vehicle was reported blocking the roadway. Multiple callers reported brush burning along eastbound Highway 58 near South Union Avenue, drawing county engines and city equipment to the grass fire.

In east Bakersfield, firefighters found light smoke at a house fire on North Kern Street. Crews were also sent to a structure fire response at a cold storage building in the 5500 block of Valpredo Avenue, where Truck 54 reported water flowing from one room and nothing from another; crews laddered the building looking for a heat source and got inside without finding anything visible.

In north Bakersfield, officers were sent to Beardsley Avenue for a disturbance involving a man on a motorized bike who was reported to be carrying a machete. He was last seen fleeing eastbound with a checkered backpack and was not located. A caller also reported impact sounds at a building on Westwind Drive in central Bakersfield, followed by a sedan leaving the area.

The rest of the log ran the usual wide range: a large debris pile burning in Wasco around 7:32 p.m., with crews calling for one additional engine and reporting power lines nearby that did not appear affected; a driver who went off the road after hitting the mountain in the canyon; a car window broken by an object thrown from a semi on Highway 166; a stolen pickup out of Los Angeles; and medical aids scattered across the county.

## Today's weather

It's 52 degrees at Meadows Field this morning, on the way to a high near 73 and a low around 50 tonight. No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County. Air quality sits at 57 — moderate — so most folks can go about their day normally, though anyone sensitive to air quality may want to keep an eye on it. Fire crews are on one active fire in Kern, the Cyrus Fire. Otherwise, it's a quiet, comfortable October day in the valley.

## Top stories

**23ABC reports that Todd Lee is back at Cal State Bakersfield as head coach of Roadrunners basketball, nearly three decades after he helped the program win a national championship.** Lee served as an assistant at CSUB from 1994 to 1997, when the Roadrunners captured the NCAA Division II title, then followed head coach Pat Douglass to UC Irvine and went on to coach at South Dakota, Kentucky Wesleyan and USC. At an open practice at the GSA Dignity Health Sports Complex, fans got a look at this year's roster. Lee told the station he has always wanted this job — "I feel like this is my home" — and said his goal is a tough, physical team and a renewed connection with a community that once packed the Icardo Center. Returning guard and forward Jaden Alexander said the culture already feels more professional.

**According to 23ABC, vandals hit Bear Mountain Park with graffiti, and part of the picnic table area is now closed off while crews work to clean it up.** The Bear Mountain Recreation and Parks District announced the vandalism on its Facebook page Oct. 9. One visitor, who gave only her first name, Maria, told the station it's sad that families can't come picnic with their kids, and that it's hard to explain to her 4-year-old son why there are writings on the playground. The district said maintenance crews have been working tirelessly to remove the damage and that it's grateful for the community's support.

**KGET 17 reports that a Kern County judge's ruling could overturn California's fracking law.** The decision, if it stands, would reach well beyond Kern County — this is the state's oil-producing heart, and fracking rules shape how local operators work and how the county's largest industry plans ahead. We'll be watching for what the ruling means in practice for Kern operators and regulators in the days to come.

**KGET 17 also reports that the Bakersfield VA clinic is moving to the former CRC headquarters on Old River, for now.** The move is described as temporary, but it matters to the thousands of local veterans who rely on the clinic for care — a change of address means a change of routine, and we'll pass along details on hours and services as they're confirmed.

**23ABC reports that Ward 1 city council candidate Mercy Peña has acknowledged two felony forgery convictions while campaigning for the seat currently held by Eric Arias.** Peña confirmed the court records are hers after the station compared signatures, and she currently serves on the Greenfield School District Board of Trustees. She told the station the convictions date to 1992, that she hasn't been expunged, and that she's owning it: "I'm going to fess up to it because it did happen." She said the experience shapes how she looks at city spending, and that her priorities include long-term recovery programs for homelessness and giving residents more say in city decisions.

**KGET 17 reports that Congressional District 20 candidate Sandra Van Scotter is talking about running as an underdog and what winning would look like for her.** We'll have more on that race as the campaign develops.

## Something good

Todd Lee's homecoming is the kind of story that gives a whole program something to rally around. He was part of the 1997 national championship staff, and now he's back where he says he belongs, talking about giving to Bakersfield because Bakersfield gives back. Fans got an early look at the roster at open practice, and there's a familiar face at the front of the gym again. Whatever the season brings, that's a good place to start.

## Coming up this week

Public meetings fill out the calendar this week. The Multi Modal Transportation and Traffic Safety Committee meets today, Tuesday, Oct. 13, at noon — a good one for anyone with thoughts on roads, bike lanes or traffic safety in the city. The Water Board meets Wednesday, Oct. 14, at 10 a.m., always worth watching in a valley that lives and works by its water. Then the Planning Commission meets Thursday, Oct. 15, at 5:30 p.m., where land-use decisions that shape neighborhoods get their first real airing.

On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater has a busy stretch. United We Dance brings festival energy for an all-night show on Friday, Oct. 16. The Boobay & Tekla Comedy Tour takes the stage Saturday, Oct. 17, and Fortune Feimster's "Taking Care of Biscuits" comedy tour lands Sunday, Oct. 18. The Cults & Classics series screens "Psycho" on Monday, Oct. 19, and Switchfoot plays with special guest Anberlin on the Forever Now Tour on Wednesday, Oct. 21. If you're planning further out, season passes for the 2026–2027 Cults & Classics series are already on sale.

Have a good Tuesday, Bakersfield. We'll see you tomorrow morning.

top.title: Todd Lee returns to CSUB with a goal of bringing Bakersfield back to Roadrunners basketball
